title: Adjunction-preserving quotient-to-pushforward support model
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and a closed immersion $a:C\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ for its open complement and set
$$Q^\tau_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!\underline A_{T\setminus C}\longrightarrow\underline A_T),\qquad \tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet},$$
where the arrow is induced by inclusion of the open object into the final object and extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Denote the quotient map by $r^\tau_{T,C}$. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with closed immersions $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$. Put $P=X\times_kY$, $S=Z\times_kW$, $h=i\times_kj$ and let $p_X,p_Y$ be the projections [def-pc-base-change]. For any one of these closed pairs $a:C\hookrightarrow T$, put
$$E_a^\tau(V)=Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_A^L\underline V_T,\qquad V\in D(A),$$
using the termwise constant sheaf and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-tensor]. Equip $E_a^\tau\dashv H_a^\tau=R\Gamma_C(T_\tau,-)$ [def-pur-support-cohomology] with the adjunction induced by the ordinary bijection sending $\sigma:Q^\tau_{T,C}\otimes_A\underline V_T\to F$ to $v\mapsto\sigma(\overline1\otimes v)$. Let $C_a(V)=a_*\underline V_C$. In the etale topology let $e_a:\underline V_T\to C_a(V)$ be the normalized quotient map of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product], and in the pro-etale topology let $q_a:\underline V_T\to C_a(V)$ be the normalized quotient map of [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product]. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\beta_a:E_a^\tau\cong C_a$ compatible with the specified adjunctions to the same right adjoint $H_a^\tau$ (the comparison on that right adjoint is the identity). It is the derived extension of the ordinary-module isomorphism whose components carry $r_a\otimes1$ to $e_a$ in the etale case and to $q_a$ in the pro-etale case. It is natural in $V$, preserves the quotient-generator maps, and identifies these adjunctions and their derived evaluation counits.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X, Y and their fibre product locally Noetherian. Apply the source finite-type instance to f, g and pullback.fst f g composed with f; this supplies the pro-etale hypotheses for all three closed pairs. Open subschemes inherit local Noetherianity through the existing open-lower-shriek instances.

proof.text: Let O -> U be the open-extension arrow defining Q, and let M be any coefficient module. Tensoring by the constant sheaf M preserves its cokernel because tensor is a left adjoint. Closed restriction of O is zero: in the etale case use disjoint-support vanishing for open extension; in the pro-etale case apply the open-extension adjunction and vanishing of the open restriction of closed direct image. Consequently the normalized map U tensor M -> a_* constant M annihilates O tensor M, and the preserved cokernel universal property constructs b_M : Q tensor M -> a_* constant M with the prescribed generator identity.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify the quotient support model with the normalized closed-pushforward support model and its counit.

proof.text: Closed inverse image is strong monoidal and sends the quotient map U -> Q to an isomorphism, since it sends O to zero and preserves cokernels. It also sends the normalized constant-to-closed-pushforward map to an isomorphism by the fully faithful closed direct-image counit and the adjunction triangle identity. The generator identity therefore makes the closed restriction of b_M invertible. Open inverse image sends the defining open-extension arrow to an isomorphism by the fully faithful open-extension unit and the triangle identity; hence it sends Q to zero. It also sends a_* constant M to zero by disjoint-support vanishing. Thus the open restriction of b_M is invertible. Joint conservativity of the open and closed restrictions proves that b_M is an isomorphism. The generator is epic, so cancellation gives naturality and uniqueness of b for arbitrary M, including nonflat modules.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify the quotient support model with the normalized closed-pushforward support model and its counit.

proof.text: Transport exactness from the existing normalized closed-pushforward coefficient functor along b. Construct the comparison on complexes as the constant exact-localization factor, the lax monoidal map of the complex-to-derived quotient, the canonical signed total-complex collapse for a degree-zero first factor, the composition isomorphism for termwise functors, and the inverse exact-localization factor. Naturality is the naturality of this composite natural transformation. This is the prescribed tensor localization comparison, with the first factor kept on the left.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify the quotient support model with the normalized closed-pushforward support model and its counit.

proof.text: Use the existing functorial flat resolution in the coefficient module category. Constant sheaves preserve flat objects by the flat-presheaf sheafification theorem. The existing flat-preserving functor theorem says that the constant image of this resolution is K-flat. The lax monoidal localization comparison is invertible when its second factor is K-flat. All the remaining factors of the comparison are isomorphisms. Its naturality square for the resolution quasi-isomorphism transports invertibility to every complex, using exactness of both coefficient functors. The universal property of localization lifts this natural isomorphism to the derived categories. No ringed-site K-flat pullback theorem or independently chosen ringed-topos resolution is needed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify the quotient support model with the normalized closed-pushforward support model and its counit.

proof.text: The quotient generator identity and the existing normalization of the supported-coefficient adjunction give the required ordinary Hom identity. For adjunctions transported along the ordinary natural isomorphism b, compare their homotopy counits after precomposing with the homotopy quotient: both reduce to the ordinary counit and b. Compare their derived counits after precomposing with Qh: the right-derived counit factorization reduces the equality to the homotopy equality. Localization extensionality proves the equality on derived categories. This uses the existing right-derived adjunction API, rather than a separate computation of Hom sets on K-injective representatives. Combining this counit transport with the tensor localization comparison gives the displayed evaluation-counit formula.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: identify the quotient support model with the normalized closed-pushforward support model and its counit.

proof.text: For any comparison preserving the specified Hom equivalences, apply the injective adjunction Hom bijection to its component followed by the identity map. The counit identity just proved shows that this component equals the constructed comparison. Conversely that identity implies the required Hom equality by naturality of the counit. The exact-functor localization factorization and the defining component formula supply the equality on every complex. Assemble the five clauses for each topology and each of i, j and the product immersion.

split_report.summary: Split the rank-one quotient using the existing etale and pro-etale open–closed sequences; extended it to arbitrary modules using free presentations and colimit-preserving adjoints; constructed the unbounded derived comparison using K-flat constant pullback; checked the derived Hom bijections on K-injectives. Corrected uniqueness to explicitly require preservation of the specified adjunctions with identity on their common right adjoint: ordinary-module components alone do not determine a natural transformation on a derived category.
